A 1-year-old clinic that markets implants, veneers and aligners and runs a paid ad is in growth mode and could pay for tools that convert more ad clicks into booked chairs, but the budget scale is unknown.

dossier.ability_to_pay: Real but thin. Observed: a paid Meta click-to-WhatsApp ad (2026-10-23), a premium-leaning service mix (implants, veneers, smile makeovers, aligners, dental tourism), 77 Google reviews in about a year, a custom multi-page site. Against that: only one ad found, library end date 2026-10-25, the Facebook page has 5 likes, the clinic is about 1 year old, and no staff or branch scale is published. Spend size and budget are unknown.
dossier.resistance: Medium. Already has a professional own website and a pre-filled WhatsApp booking flow, so the core campaign pitch (website + WhatsApp button) is redundant. The site looks developer- or tool-built, so a vendor or in-house helper may exist (builder not credited). No public stance against bots or AI. The owner is a practising prosthodontist (hard to reach in clinic hours), and it is unclear whether the published number is the doctor's or the front desk's.
dossier.case_for: Verified real, independent, owner-led clinic in the right city (Ahmedabad). Dr. Gunjan Thakur is named, and the clinic publishes a WhatsApp/phone number, a second phone and an email. It is spending on a click-to-WhatsApp ad right now (anniversary offer till 31 Oct), so WhatsApp is its chosen lead channel and there is a plausible, still-unproven gap in instant after-hours auto-replies. The Google profile does not link its website, which shows its online setup is not fully joined up.
dossier.case_against: The campaign need is wrong for this lead. It already has a professional site with SEO pages and a WhatsApp booking button, and a well-reviewed, claimed Google profile, so 'no website / weak presence' is false and the finder's evidence rested on an unchecked 'no website on Maps'. The only remaining need (auto-answered WhatsApp) is purely inferred, with no evidence of slow or manual replies. Pay signal is one short-lived ad and a 5-like page. It may have a site vendor. A pitch that says 'you have no website' would be factually wrong and would burn the lead.
dossier.best_angle: Do not lead with a website or 'no website' (false). If we touch it at all, use a narrow WhatsApp-automation angle tied to their own ad: the anniversary offer ad sends patients into WhatsApp, so offer an instant auto-reply (treatment menu, slot booking, after-hours answer) on the number they already use, and mention in one line that the Google profile does not link their website. Better still, move this lead out of the 'no-website clinics' campaign into a separate 'WhatsApp auto-reply for clinics running click-to-WhatsApp ads' campaign. The offer expires 31 Oct, so timing is short.
dossier.best_channel: Email to the published address (amicadentalstudio@gmail.com), then a human phone call to the published number if the owner approves. Do not cold-template WhatsApp (0/3 so far) and do not use the clinic's own enquiry button as a patient.
gaps: I could not open the Meta ad page directly (403 / login wall); ad details come from an Apify ad-library actor, so the real ad status after 2026-10-25 is unconfirmed.

Pipeline lesson: a finder rule of 'Maps listing has no website' needs a follow-up check for the business name plus a domain before it is treated as 'has no website'.
